title: First Modern Restoration — Ohel Rebuilt
description: Following the collapse of Soviet restrictions, the first organized restoration visits to Lubavitch took place. The Ohel covering the graves of the Tzemach Tzedek and the Rebbe Maharash — damaged during World War II and neglected for decades — was rebuilt. Initial cleaning and preservation work was carried out at the cemetery by Reb Dovid Nachshon and Reb Avi Taub.

title: Schneerson House Purchased
description: A large house in Lyubavichi was purchased and registered in the name of Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson. The building has since served as a guest house and small museum, providing accommodation and information for the growing number of pilgrims visiting Lubavitch.

title: Information Center Opens: Hatzer Raboteinu
description: The information center 'Hatzer Raboteinu Nesieinu Belubavitch' (The Courtyard of Our Rebbeim in Lubavitch) opened on the historic site of the Rebbe's courtyard. The center documents the 102-year history of Chabad leadership in Lubavitch with maps, photographs, and historical materials.

title: 500 European Rabbis Pilgrimage to Lubavitch
description: The European Conference of Shluchim brought approximately 500 Chabad rabbis to Lubavitch for a historic gathering at the Ohel. The visit — the largest organized group to travel to Lubavitch in modern times — drew international attention to the village and accelerated calls for further restoration.

title: Cemetery Fencing Project — Geder Avos Partnership Begins
description: The Geder Avos organization established a formal partnership with Rabbi Gavriel Gordon to undertake systematic restoration of the Lubavitch cemetery. A new protective fence was constructed around the cemetery perimeter. The project is fully sponsored by Yosef and Penina Batsheva Popack.

title: Foundation of the Original Shul Uncovered
description: During excavation work adjacent to the Ohel, workers discovered the original foundation of the Akeda Shul — the synagogue that bordered the graves of the Tzemach Tzedek and Rebbe Maharash. Rabbi Gavriel Gordon confirmed this was the shul where the Frierdiker Rebbe delivered his last Maamar in Russia in 1922. A four-year rebuilding project began immediately.

title: Hundreds of Matzeivos Uncovered and Reinstalled
description: Working systematically through the cemetery, the Geder Avos team and Rabbi Gavriel Gordon uncovered hundreds of matzeivos that had been buried, tipped, or overgrown. Each stone was raised, cleaned, and reinstalled in its proper location. A full database was then compiled documenting every grave in the Lubavitch cemetery — names, dates, and Hebrew inscriptions.

title: Ohel of the Rebbetzins Rebuilt
description: A new Ohel structure was constructed over the resting places of the wives and daughters of the Chabad Rebbeim. The rebuilding restored dignity to the site and ensured proper identification and access for visitors honoring these pivotal figures in Chabad history.

title: Akeda Shul Fully Restored and Reopened
description: After four years of careful reconstruction, the Akeda Shul was returned to full functionality with an Aron Kodesh, Bima, a library with Chabad seforim, and dedicated spaces for prayer and study. Groups of visitors now use the shul regularly on their pilgrimages to Lubavitch. The nistarim cemetery was also demarcated and fenced during this period.

title: Ohel of the Rebbeim — Major Renovation
description: A major renovation of the Ohel of the Tzemach Tzedek and Rebbe Maharash was completed, including structural preservation, improvements to the surrounding grounds, and enhanced visitor access. Coordinated by Rabbi Gavriel Gordon, this was the most significant investment in the primary Ohel since the 1989 rebuilding.
